summary:
Implemented the terminal window title feature by reading and editing files only; nothing was run or committed.

Changes:
- rich/segment.py: added SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 to ControlType and Tuple[ControlType, str] to the ControlCode union.
- rich/control.py: added the formatting-table entry emitting ESC ] 0 ; title BEL, and the Control.title(title) classmethod with a docstring.
- rich/_windows_renderer.py: added a dispatch branch that calls term.set_title(title) for SET_WINDOW_TITLE controls.
- rich/console.py: added set_window_title(title) -> bool beside show_cursor. It buffers a title control and returns True when is_terminal, otherwise False. Google-style docstring covers the restore, reset, and return-value caveats.
- CHANGELOG.md: one Unreleased "Added" bullet linking pull request 2200.
- tests/test_console.py: test_set_window_title (skipped on win32), asserting the sequence and a True return.
- tests/test_control.py: test_control_title, checking segment text, no style, and the control list.
- tests/test_windows_renderer.py: test_control_set_window_title (Windows only), asserting set_title is called with "Hello, world!".

Not verified: tests, mypy, and black were not run, per the instructions. Verification was by reading only.

Choices: the OSC number is 0, which sets both icon and window title. The Windows test skip follows the existing skipif(sys.platform == "win32") convention.

Nothing is committed.
